messages:
Maria G.: heads up — customer reported repeated 401s from Python SDK when retries are enabled, started after yesterday's client push :eyes:
AJ: ugh. which sdk version and which API call?
Maria G.: python client v0.9.2, call is `client.responses.create(...)` with token in `Authorization` header. repro steps below:
```
# minimal repro
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = c.responses.create(model='redwood-v1', input='hi')
print(resp)
```
Maria G.: log shows retry loop then 401 consistently:
```
[2026-03-01T14:02:03Z] DEBUG retrying request attempt=1 url=/v1/responses status=401
[2026-03-01T14:02:03Z] DEBUG retrying request attempt=2 url=/v1/responses status=401
[2026-03-01T14:02:03Z] ERROR auth failed token=***
```
Samir K.: interesting — OpenAPI spec change landed last night: security scheme name went from `apiKeyAuth` -> `bearerAuth` in openapi.yaml, generator mapping broke header wiring. I saw the regen job failed but got merged somehow. :thinking_face:
Elaine: i noticed the regen CI job errored with `path not found: /docs/openapi.yaml` but merge proceeded after a quick rebase. ci-bot posted the failure: <https://ci.internal/12345|build #12345>
ci-bot: Build #12345 failed: openapi-regeneration (exit 2) — missing spec path
AJ: so the client generator didn't pick up the new security scheme mapping; that would explain missing header code. Can someone confirm the generated `auth.py`?
Chris: grabbing a copy from pip wheel on customer env — here's the header helper in v0.9.2:
```
def _auth_headers():
    return { }
```
Chris: yep empty dict, so client isn't sending `Authorization` at all when using the auth helper path.
Samir K.: root cause: openapi change + regen job silently produced a client with a todo placeholder. The regen script has a conditional that skips security if `x-internal` flag is present — spec added flag by mistake.
AJ: can we hotpatch a quick release? recommended fix: regenerate with updated mapping and bump to 0.9.3, or patch runtime to read `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and set header if generator missed it.
Maria G.: customer is on Dedicated and seeing errors on production; this is P1 for support. Need rollback or patch asap.
Elaine: i'll open a PR to pin the previous working client template and re-run regen today. pushing minimal runtime guard now (adds fallback header) — PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-python/pulls/456 :shipit:
Chris: quick patch snippet I'm deploying to edge to protect other clients:
```
# fallback auth in runtime
if not headers.get('Authorization') and os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'):
    headers['Authorization'] = f"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}"
```
AJ: good. also let's add a regression test: assert requests include Authorization header for generated client with env key. I'll add to ci integration tests.
Samir K.: i also found a changelog gap — the openapi change wasn't listed in the generator notes. will add entry and blame the automated spec bump PR.
Maria G.: thanks team. next steps: (1) rollback bad client release from package index, (2) push runtime fallback patch to hosted and dedicated pools, (3) re-run openapi regen with corrected flags and publish 0.9.3, (4) add CI test to prevent missing auth in future. i'll coordinate with support and notify customer. :raised_hands:
AJ: tagging infra to monitor latency and error spikes during rollout @ops — watch for 401/5xx backoff storms.
ci-bot: Deployment started for runtime-fallback patch — deploy/789
Elaine: deploying rollback branch for the client wheel to pypi staging. will update thread when done.
Maria G.: leaving notes for support: repro steps, temporary workaround (set `Authorization` header manually or set `REDWOOD_API_KEY`), ETA for patch ~45m.
Chris: postmortem todo: add linter to regen job to fail if security schemes change without changelog entry.
Maria G.: 👍 thanks all, will post status updates in this thread.
